title: Cozy Oaks - a cozy farming game for these stressful times
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3KJwgGv_hq0

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *Cozy Oaks*, the new farming game from Peter Jank, designer of Quest for the Lost Pixel. It's pitched as what your adventurer does after retiring from dungeons. Daniel discloses that the two are friends: Peter lives nearby, came over to play it, and left this copy. It's available through The Game Crafter, and the neoprene mats on show are an optional extra.

Inspired by Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon and Cult of the Lamb, it's a competitive game for one or two players, played over three years of seasons. You inherit a run-down farm with a broken greenhouse and windmill, a weedy field, and a coop and barn full of poop. Each skill card does a job: improve, farm, livestock, craft, cook, forage, mine, hunt slimes or fish. Foraging, mining and slime-hunting feed set collection, while fishing is a majority race.

The clever part is time. Every skill card shows a clock cost paid by discarding other cards, and the sleep card upgrades a skill each time you rest, so specialising makes each action eat more of your hand. Early turns are broad and leisurely, and later ones narrow and quick. Players also move through the seasons at their own pace. In the solo mode, a villager deck adds restrictions, end-of-year requests and a friendship threshold you must hold.

Daniel admits it's not usually his kind of game, but says it's exactly the weight he enjoys when he does play one: snappy, pleasant and genuinely cozy.

----

Do cozy farming games tempt you onto the table, or do you need monsters in the mix to stay interested?
